@Ryan Casey similar question re: meaning of the icon in there and possibly the need to add " (opens new tab)" to the end of the button's name (i.e. via 'aria-label' or 'title' - the latter one would show a tooltip on hover which is preferable for sighted users too)

@Ryan Casey would that button open a new tab? the icon in it indicates so, but if this would technically only navigate to another sub-page within about:logins, it may not be needed?

if it does navigate to other page, even within about pages, i.e. to about:preferences, we'd need to include the alt text for this button in the button's accessible name, i.e. "Name: 'Change password (opens new tab)'" or similar.

Eng note:  It could be done via 'aria-label' on the button or 'title' - the latter one would show a tooltip on hover which is preferable for sighted users too.

General Note: the Acorns team was working on the links with this addition " (opens new tab)", so maybe that component is available for buttons too (and it has the text alternative already)
@Ryan Casey I also increased this spacing to 24 so the text beneath had a little more breathing room

@Ryan Casey i sketched out a few options to address the the clash of red header background with the card drop shadow

• Option 1: red border on the header section
•Option 2: a transparent border on the card
Option 3: inset the header section

Dismiss is primary, see additional steps as secondary

Missing opportunity to celebrate user making positive security change.
Cant win here, as its another notification.
you've updated your password, and you can still do more to protect yourself.

@Ryan Casey one thing to note in the current designs, breached sites are brought to the top in their own section and then there is a section for no alerts. I think it would be good to keep this pattern right?

@Ryan Casey I know there was the risk of the cognitive load with there being 3 buttons but I'm wondering if this now just being a text link lowers its importance too much. I think we're aligned primary action is change password. With this being a secondary action, the button did seem okay because the accordion was closed. I'm a bit nervous in this treatment it will feel like a user is just being taken to a blog post or some sort of static page. @Laura Lopez I'm also wondering if we want the content to be more actionable because we want users to take steps.
icon spacing a little funky
Is "Mark as Fixed" accurate, or would be "Dismiss" be more accurate?

@Brooke Katalinich  I think this i what you were referring to when we chatted about this. I feel like this experience is very disjointed and would also be really bad for accessibility - especially users using magnification, or users with cognative impairments.

@Ryan Casey I'm still struggling some with the layouts. Is it worth a combination of these elements:

1. Colored alert at top of above content, to the right?
2. Contextual state higlighted
3. No stroked on the card, and a light bg with white cards or lines only at the top.

@Ryan Casey I think this image could be made informative: visually it communicates attention/warning, so it could announce "Warning:" or "Important:" for screen reader users too.
Thank you for adding an in-context reference too <3 @Ryan Casey

@Ryan Casey and in this case, only the disclosure control (the first row item) would have the HCM colors since it is the only clickable area to expand/collapse the section, plus that the collapsible panel has its own button - we want to avoid having interactive areas overlap, on HCM especially. Thus, the bottom/collapsible area would stay the same here (keeping the Canvas/CanvasText aka black/white colors)

@Ryan Casey this would be a disclosure button (or details/summary element, depending on the code behind it), thus we'd need ButtonText/ButtonBackground colors for HCM - the same as the "Change password" (secondary button) looks like

@Ryan Casey here the actual font color seems off-white and gets the color contrast against the button's background to 4.3:1 which is right below the threshold of 4.5:1 (seems easier to read than the thinner text for "7 types of data exposed" and the link above - both are technically WCAG 2.2 Level AA compliant, but technically need a bit of a toggle)

@Ryan Casey TL;DR: the link has low color contrast against the background here...

I'm not sure why.... is the link color correct? the eyedropper tool shows its #3178E1 and the color contrast with the lighter red is 3.7:1 (min 4.5:1 is needed)? Maybe there is a transparency in play for the text or something similar?

You think it's getting too red with this red on red look? Almost too loud? Curious if you thought about only relying on the icon having red or maybe only the exposure details.

We don't support coloring the box today so I'll float that to engineering too.
